pages.title: MDS admin commands: admin socket and tell

features.name: Local admin socket transport
features.description: Unix socket at admin_socket ($run_dir/$cluster-$name.asok); request is a JSON command string (<=1023 bytes) terminated by NUL or newline, legacy 4-byte codes 0/1/2; reply is 4-byte big-endian length + payload, errors prefixed 'ERROR: <strerror>' because the rc is not transmitted. One admin_socket thread; local requests wait synchronously for asynchronous commands.
features.notes: Used by `ceph daemon`, ceph-exporter and qa (rank_asok/mds_asok). No cephx; file permissions only.

features.name: Remote tell transport (MCommand/MCommandReply)
features.description: MCommand (97: fsid, vector<string> cmd, data=inbl) handled under mds_lock by MDSDaemon::handle_command, queued to the AdminSocket tell queue and executed asynchronously on the admin thread; MCommandReply (98: errorcode32 r, rs, data=outbl, tid echoed) sent from the completing thread.
features.notes: Commands on a reset connection are dropped without reply. Legacy MMonCommand 'mds tell' is dropped with a clog warning.

features.name: Tell authorization
features.description: Remote commands require MDSAuthCaps::allow_all(): some grant whose spec is '*' (or 'all') and whose match has no path and no uid (uid=0 counts as any); the grant's fsname= and root_squash are NOT checked, so 'allow * fsname=a' may tell the MDS daemons of every file system. Otherwise -EACCES 'permission denied'. Command-only (non-SessionMap) connections are marked disposable.
features.notes: mgr and client.admin get mds 'allow *' from cephadm.

features.name: Command self-description (get_command_descriptions, help)
features.description: AdminSocket built-ins return descriptor signatures {cmdNNN:{sig,help}} for every registered command; the ceph CLI fetches them before every tell/daemon command and validates arguments locally (CephChoices n=N comma splitting, '--' named-only args).
features.notes: Without this the stock CLI cannot address the daemon at all.

features.name: Argument validation, formatting and output-file
features.description: cmdmap_from_json, exact prefix lookup, validate_cmd (required scalar args, ranges, choices; vector args never required; unknown keys ignored); format json/json-pretty/xml/table/html (fallback json-pretty); output-file writes JSON on the daemon host; formatter flushed only when r>=0 and no explicit output.
features.notes: Error JSON written to the formatter is discarded when r<0 unless the handler flushes it itself.

features.name: Client-side target resolution for tell
features.description: libcephfs Client::mds_command resolves role <fs>:<rank> (or bare rank of legacy fs), gid, name or '*' against the latest FSMap; skips laggy targets; one_shot aborts with -EPIPE on reset/refused; commands to targets that go DNE/laggy are cancelled with -ETIMEDOUT; multi-target output aggregated as [{mds.<name>: out}].
features.notes: Requires the MDS to be correctly represented in the FSMap (name, gid, addrs, rank, state, laggy).

features.name: status
features.description: Daemon and rank status: cluster_fsid, whoami, id, want_state, state, fs_name, state-specific replay/resolve/reconnect/rejoin/clientreplay status, rank_uptime, mdsmap/osdmap epochs, osdmap_epoch_barrier, uptime, sysinfo, endian.
features.notes: qa wait_for_daemons requires state=='up:active' for active ranks; docs use `status | jq .replay_status`.

features.name: Process control: exit, respawn, lockup
features.description: exit -> suicide() after 1 s; respawn -> execv self after 1 s (same PID); lockup sleeps holding mds_lock (dev).
features.notes: cephtool workunit uses `ceph tell mds.0 respawn`.

features.name: heap and cpu_profiler
features.description: tcmalloc heap profiler commands (-EOPNOTSUPP without tcmalloc) and gperftools CPU profiler control.
features.notes: mgr telemetry perf channel (opt-in) sends `heap stats` and tolerates failure.

features.name: Op tracker dumps
features.description: dump_ops_in_flight, ops [--flags=locks] [--path], dump_blocked_ops(_count), dump_historic_ops(_by_duration): TrackedOp dumps of client, peer and internal MDRequests; only ops/op get with --flags=locks take mds_lock.
features.notes: Documented in troubleshooting; qa TestValidTell checks JSON validity.

features.name: op get / op kill
features.description: Look up an MDRequest by reqid <entity>.<num>:<tid> and dump it, or kill it via MDCache::request_kill (requests involving peers are only marked aborted). Releases lock path / quiesce path ops.

features.name: session ls / client ls
features.description: List client sessions (optionally filtered) as Session::dump: id, auth_name, entity, state, num_leases, num_caps, request_load_avg, uptime, counters, recall/release decay counters, delegated/prealloc inos, completed_requests, inst, client_metadata (client_features, metric_spec, all kv).
features.notes: Peer-critical: dashboard (session ls, format json, target <fscid>:0) and mgr/stats (client ls to rank 0; needs hostname, root, metric_spec.metric_flags.feature_bits).

features.name: session evict / client evict
features.description: Evict every client session matching a SessionFilter: mon 'osd blocklist add <addr>' (if mds_session_blocklist_on_evict), wait for latest OSDMap, set osd_epoch_barrier, journal session kill; reply when all kills completed; -EAGAIN during replay; 'no hosts match' rc 0.
features.notes: Peer-critical: mgr/volumes `fs subvolume evict` (auth_name + client_metadata.root filters, per rank by gid) and dashboard (id=<n>, <fscid>:0). qa uses the bare-id form `session evict <id>`. An empty filter list, `id=*` (which stops parsing; earlier criteria still apply) or a bare `0` evicts every client of the rank; id= values outside the 32-bit int range are rejected by a std::stoi pre-check.

features.name: session kill
features.description: Evict one session by id synchronously (blocks the admin thread across blocklist round trip and journaled kill).
features.notes: Debug only; no consumer in tree.

features.name: session config / client config timeout
features.description: Set or remove client_metadata['timeout'] (value checked with strtoul base 0, stored as given). Affects only open sessions already past session_timeout in find_idle_sessions: 0 = never mark stale, otherwise evict directly (no stale) once cap-renew age >= timeout + dispatch-queue age; session_autoclose (300 s default) still evicts first. Sessions with the key are kept at reconnect for reclaim. Not marked dirty.
features.notes: The same metadata key is set by libcephfs session timeout APIs used by NFS-Ganesha (see sessions page).

features.name: Scrub control (start, abort, pause, resume, status, purge_status)
features.description: Rank-0-coordinated forward scrub: start enqueues ENQUEUE_SCRUB (rc always 0, outcome in return_code), abort/pause/resume broadcast MMDSScrub to other ranks, status reports per-tag scrubs and uninline stats; purge_status drops stats. scrub resume reports return_code 1 (bool conversion of -EINVAL in ScrubStack::scrub_resume) while an abort is pending, else 0.
features.notes: Documented operator procedure targeting mds.<fs>:0; qa scrub tests.

features.name: tag path and scrub_tag xattr
features.description: Recursive forced scrub with a user tag; writes xattr scrub_tag on each inode's first object for cephfs-data-scan --filter-tag; admin thread waits for the enqueue.
features.notes: Only meaningful with C++-compatible data layout tools.

features.name: scrub_path (dead command)
features.description: Registered prefix with no handler branch; always -ENOSYS. scrub_start handler is unreachable.
features.notes: Artifact of commit 8a2f2625799.

features.name: damage ls / damage rm
features.description: In-memory DamageTable listing (dir_frag, dentry, backtrace, uninline entries with random ids) and removal; non-empty table raises MDS_HEALTH_DAMAGE.
features.notes: Documented in damaged-rank.rst.

features.name: flush journal
features.description: Seal current segment with ESubtreeMap, flush and wait safe, expire all older segments (writing back dirty metadata), write journal head; -EROFS if read-only; no-op on non-active ranks; JSON {message, return_code}.
features.notes: Documented in disaster-recovery.rst; most used qa command.

features.name: flush_path
features.description: Internal FLUSH op: write back one inode's backtrace and parent dirfrag; -EXDEV on non-auth rank (internal ops not forwarded).
features.notes: Used by qa (qa/tasks/cephfs/test_scrub_checks.py:263-289); not debug-only.

features.name: force_readonly
features.description: Make the rank read-only until restart: sends CEPH_SESSION_FORCE_RO to all clients, re-evaluates caps to revoke write caps, flushes log; also triggered by write errors with mds_action_on_write_error=1.
features.notes: Kernel sets s_readonly and fails Fw/Fx cap acquisition with -EROFS.

features.name: osdmap barrier
features.description: Set osd_epoch_barrier to a given epoch (may lower it) and block the admin thread until the Objecter has that epoch.
features.notes: qa test_full.

features.name: cache drop
features.description: Recall caps from all clients (RECALL_STATE + FLUSHMSG, re-armed every 1 s until done or timeout), flush journal, trim cache; report client_recall, flush_journal, trim_cache, cache, duration.
features.notes: timeout=0 waits indefinitely for client acks. If the inner C_Flush_Journal fails (e.g. -EROFS on a read-only rank), cmd_err closes the formatter's only section and C_Drop_Cache::finish closes it again, tripping ceph_assert(!m_stack.empty()) in JSONFormatter::close_section: the daemon aborts (inferred from code, not observed).

features.name: cache status / dump cache
features.description: mds_co mempool stats; full cache dump to JSON (bounded by 1 GiB threshold and timeout <= beacon interval) or plain-text file (O_EXCL) on the MDS host, under mds_lock.
features.notes: dump cache documented in troubleshooting.rst.

features.name: Cache object dumps: dump tree, dump inode, dump dir, openfiles ls
features.description: Cache-only dumps of a subtree (post-order), a single inode by number, a directory's fragments, and inodes with wanted caps on log segments' open file lists.
features.notes: Use cache_traverse, never load from RADOS.

features.name: dump stray
features.description: Scan all stray directories (fetching incomplete dirfrags) and dump primary stray inodes as a bare JSON array of {"ino: ", "stray_prior_path: ", caps dump} (empty output when there are none); marks STATE_STRAY/STATE_ORPHAN.
features.notes: Documented in scrub.rst.

features.name: dump loads
features.description: Balancer view: dirfrags[] (breadth-first, meta_load >= 0.001), mds_load per rank, mds_meta_load, mds_import_map; nothing else.

features.name: dump snaps
features.description: SnapClient cached snap table or (with --server, table-server rank only) the SnapServer table.
features.notes: Used by qa/workunits/fs/damage/test-first-damage.sh (last_created).

features.name: get subtrees
features.description: Subtree map with authority, export pins (static, distributed/random ephemeral) and CDir dump of each subtree root.
features.notes: Widely used by qa to find auth ranks (dir.path, dir.dir_auth, auth_first).

features.name: export dir / dump_export_states
features.description: Manually start a subtree export to a rank (fire-and-forget, many silent no-op conditions, rc 0) and dump in-progress export state machines.

features.name: dirfrag split / merge / ls
features.description: Manually split or merge a cached auth dirfrag (errors only in status string) and list fragtree leaves.

features.name: lock path
features.description: Test hook: internal LOCK_PATH op takes named r/w/x locks on an inode and holds them until op kill or lifetime; options ap_dont_block, ap_freeze, await.
features.notes: Continuous op, excluded from slow request warnings. Used by qa test_quiesce/test_subvolume. Without --await no internal_op_finish is installed, so any failure (traversal error, bad lock spec, ap_dont_block conflict) hits ceph_abort_msg in Server::respond_to_request (inferred from code, not observed).

features.name: quiesce path
features.description: Test hook: internal QUIESCE_PATH op quiesces a subtree; replies immediately or with --await on completion; released by op kill.
features.notes: -EAGAIN on a non-active rank. Without --await, a synchronous completion frees the context via respond_to_request while mdr->internal_op_finish still points at it; command_quiesce_path then calls finish() on it (use-after-free, usually benign; inferred from code).

features.name: quiesce db
features.description: Front end to the QuiesceDbManager (leader only, else -ENOTTY with {epoch, leader}); include/exclude/reset/release/query/cancel of quiesce sets with timeout/expiration/await semantics; replies from the manager thread.
features.notes: Peer-critical: mgr/volumes `fs quiesce` (passes extra keys; retries on -ENOTTY using output 'leader', at most 5 attempts). On -ENOTTY the body is {epoch: MDSMap epoch, leader: gid}; -EFAULT without a manager; validation errors -EINVAL with status text only.

features.name: quarantine enable / disable
features.description: Start internal QUARANTINEDIR_AUTH op on a subvolume root: traversal errors (e.g. -ENOENT), -EXDEV when this rank is not auth for the root inode (inode authority follows the dirfrag holding its dentry; internal ops are not forwarded), -EINVAL if not a subvolume root, -EBUSY if an op is in progress, 0 if already in the requested state; reply {return_code, operation, status, error?}, rc = return_code.
features.notes: Peer-critical: mgr/volumes `fs subvolume quarantine enable|disable` (sent to the first active rank in sorted mdsmap.up, normally rank 0, which works while that rank is auth for the /volumes/<group> dirfrag holding the subvolume dentry).

features.name: QoS commands (dump qos, qos set/rm/get)
features.description: Per-rank, in-memory dmClock QoS overrides keyed by subvolume root derived from session client_metadata.root; qos set/rm return_code 1 = success, rc always 0.
features.notes: Documented in mds-qos.rst; no qa coverage.

features.name: Task status to mgr (scrub status)
features.description: Every mds_task_status_update_interval the rank pushes {'scrub status': summary} via MgrClient while scrubbing (one empty map when it returns to idle); shown in ceph -s 'task status' and ceph service dump.

features.name: Extraordinary-event in-memory log dumps
features.description: Optional timer dumping recent in-memory logs after client evictions, missed beacon acks or missed internal heartbeats (mds_extraordinary_events_dump_interval).

features.name: Generic perf/counter/config/log commands
features.description: CephContext commands present in every daemon: perf dump/schema/histogram/reset, counter dump/schema, config show/help/set/unset/get/diff, injectargs, log flush/dump/reopen, legacy perfcounters_*.
features.notes: ceph-exporter uses counter dump, counter schema, config show (pid_file); qa uses perf dump, config get/set, injectargs.

features.name: dump_mempools
features.description: Mempool statistics {mempool{by_pool{<pool>{items,bytes}}, total}}.
features.notes: mgr telemetry perf channel.

features.name: rotate-key / wipe-rotating-secrets
features.description: MonClient asok commands: replace the daemon's live cephx key from a base64 input buffer; wipe rotating secrets.
features.notes: cephadm _rotate_daemon_key would call `ceph tell mds.<name> rotate-key -i -`, falling back to restart; dormant in this tree.

features.name: Version and ping built-ins (0, version, git_version)
features.description: '0' returns CEPH_ADMIN_SOCK_VERSION '2' (ceph-exporter liveness ping), version returns {version, release, release_type}.

features.name: objecter_requests, messenger dump, raise
features.description: Objecter in-flight OSD ops, messenger state, signal delivery.
features.notes: Debug.

features.name: Metrics path and rbytes lookups under mds_lock
features.description: MDSRank::get_path (from MetricsHandler::handle_payload on the messenger dispatch thread, MetricsHandler being its own Dispatcher) and get_inode_rbytes (from update_rank0 on the MetricsHandler updater thread) take mds_lock for one inode lookup each.

features.name: JSON output conventions of the admin formatter
features.description: The JSONFormatter drops section names at top level, so the outermost object/array name never appears (cache status -> {pool:{...}}, get subtrees/session ls -> bare arrays, qos get -> bare VolumeInfo); XML keeps names. Formatter output is discarded when r < 0 unless the handler flushes it itself.
features.notes: Consumers parse these exact shapes (mgr/stats, dashboard, qa TestValidTell).

serialization_points.name: Single admin_socket thread
serialization_points.shared_state: AdminSocket hook invocation; local asok synchronous completion wait
serialization_points.why_serialized: One thread serves all asok connections and the tell queue; local asok requests block it until async completion; several handlers block it (osdmap barrier, session kill, tag path, lockup).
serialization_points.notes: A blocked or slow command delays perf dump, status and every other admin request of the process.

serialization_points.name: mds_lock taken by most rank admin handlers
serialization_points.shared_state: MDCache, SessionMap, subtree map, ScrubStack, DamageTable, snap tables, Migrator, dmClock state
serialization_points.why_serialized: Big lock protects all rank state; every handler simply takes it.
serialization_points.notes: True scopes: session (session ls/evict/config), inode/dirfrag (dump inode/dir, dirfrag, flush_path), subtree (export dir), journal (flush journal), damage table, scrub state.

serialization_points.name: MCommand admission under mds_lock
serialization_points.shared_state: Connection priv Session, SessionMap lookup for liveness
serialization_points.why_serialized: All dispatch goes through ms_dispatch2 which takes mds_lock before handle_core_message.
serialization_points.notes: Admission only needs the connection's session and caps.

serialization_points.name: Whole-cache walks under mds_lock
serialization_points.why_serialized: Iteration stability while dumping; dump cache bounded by timeout <= mds_beacon_interval (default half of it).
serialization_points.notes: Also dump tree /, openfiles ls, dump loads, dump stray scans; read-only.

serialization_points.name: force_readonly mode switch
serialization_points.shared_state: readonly flag, every head inode's cap locks, all client sessions
serialization_points.why_serialized: Rank-wide mode change that must revoke write caps everywhere.

serialization_points.name: flush journal
serialization_points.why_serialized: Seals and expires every segment of the rank journal and writes the head.
serialization_points.notes: Conflicts only with other writers of the same journal.

serialization_points.name: cache drop recall/trim
serialization_points.shared_state: Recall throttles, all sessions' caps, cache LRU, journal

serialization_points.name: Eviction blocklist/barrier/kill
serialization_points.why_serialized: Blocklist must be in the OSDMap before the session is killed; barrier advertised to other clients.
serialization_points.notes: Ordering per session is inherent; the barrier value is rank-wide but monotonic in practice.

serialization_points.name: Scrub control on rank 0
serialization_points.shared_state: ScrubStack state, scrubbing_map tags, per-tag stats, MMDSScrub broadcast

serialization_points.name: lock path / quiesce path internal ops
serialization_points.why_serialized: They exist to take real locks.

serialization_points.name: quarantine op registry
serialization_points.why_serialized: One quarantine operation per subvolume root at a time (-EBUSY).

serialization_points.name: Metrics path/rbytes lookups
serialization_points.why_serialized: MetricsHandler thread takes mds_lock for lookups.

serialization_points.name: AdminSocket hook unregistration under mds_lock
serialization_points.shared_state: AdminSocket hooks map, process-wide in_hook flag
serialization_points.why_serialized: suicide() holds mds_lock while unregister_commands waits for in_hook to clear; a hook blocked on mds_lock in the admin thread would deadlock (inferred).
serialization_points.notes: in_hook is cleared when call_async returns, not when an async command completes.

external_contract.detail: JSON command string terminated by NUL or newline (<=1023 bytes), reply = 4-byte big-endian length + payload; negative rc only visible as 'ERROR: ...' prefix; legacy 4-byte codes 0/1/2.
Scans exporter_sock_dir for *.asok; ping {"prefix":"0"} expects 1-byte reply; counter dump + counter schema (type, metric_type, description, priority, labels) and config show pid_file.
MCommand(97): fsid, vector<string> cmd JSON, data=inbl; MCommandReply(98): errorcode32 r (Linux errno on wire), rs, data; tid echoed; no reply for commands on reset connections.
MDS cap grant 'allow *' with no path and no uid required (fsname= and root_squash are not checked); else -EACCES 'permission denied'.
ceph CLI fetches {cmdNNN:{sig,help}} before every tell/daemon command and validates args locally; descriptor types decide comma splitting (CephChoices n=N) and named-only args ('--').
Targets: name, gid, role <fs>:<rank>, legacy bare rank, '*'; laggy targets skipped; -ETIMEDOUT when target goes DNE/laggy; one_shot -EPIPE on reset/refused.
Array of sessions with id, client_metadata.hostname, root (required), mount_point and kernel_version (optional), metric_spec.metric_flags.feature_bits hex string; sent to rank 0 gid of every fs.
format=json, target <fscid>:0; uses id, state, client_metadata ceph_version/kernel_version/hostname/root.
filters=['id=<n>'] to <fscid>:0; rc only.
filters=['auth_name=<id>','client_metadata.root=<subvolume path>'] to every up rank by gid via mounted libcephfs; retried on -ETIMEDOUT; waits for up:active/up:clientreplay.

Whole volumes kwargs dict plus roots and prefix (extra keys must be ignored); one_shot to mdsmap.qdb_leader by gid; on -ENOTTY parse JSON 'leader' and retry (at most 5 attempts in total); JSON passed through to the user.

{prefix, path=/volumes/<group|_nogroup>/<subvol>} to the first up:active/up:clientreplay entry of sorted mdsmap.up (normally rank 0); that rank must be auth for the subvolume root inode or the MDS returns -EXDEV; reply {return_code, operation, status, error?}.
heap heapcmd=stats parsed for 'tcmalloc heap stats' and 12 integers; dump_mempools format=json mempool.by_pool.<pool>.{bytes,items}; failures only logged; perf channel opt-in.
`ceph tell mds.<name> rotate-key -i -` with base64 key; on failure cephadm would restart the daemon; helper has no caller and orch daemon rotate-key is disabled in this tree.
MMgrReport.task_status {'scrub status': summary} pushed every 2 s while non-idle, one empty map when idle again; shown by ceph -s and ceph service dump.
Mon command {"prefix":"osd blocklist","blocklistop":"add","addr":"<addr>"} (no expiry), then wait for latest OSDMap and set osd_epoch_barrier before killing the session; result ignored.
Kernel sets session s_readonly; later Fw/Fx cap acquisition fails with -EROFS; libcephfs force_session_readonly.

external_contract.item: RECALL_STATE and FLUSHMSG from cache drop
external_contract.detail: RECALL_STATE with max_caps (kernel ceph_trim_caps) and FLUSHMSG (kernel flushes cap releases, replies FLUSHMSG_ACK) gathered by the MDS.
Tagged scrubs (scrub start with tag, tag path) set xattr scrub_tag (encoded string) on <ino>.00000000 in the backtrace pool; cephfs-data-scan --filter-tag reads it.

TestValidTell requires valid JSON from cache status, damage ls, dump_blocked_ops(_count), dump_historic_ops(_by_duration), dump_mempools, dump_ops_in_flight, flush journal, get subtrees, ops locks, ops, status, version; wait_for_daemons checks status.state=='up:active'; many tests use flush journal, session ls/evict, get subtrees, scrub, damage, dump inode/tree, cache drop, lock/quiesce path, op get/kill.

ceph tell mds.<fs>:0 scrub start|status|abort|pause|resume, flush journal, damage ls|rm, client ls|evict, dump stray, status, qos set|get|rm|dump qos; ceph daemon mds.<name> dump cache <file>, dump_ops_in_flight.
Rook is believed to probe MDS liveness via the admin socket; Rook source is not in this tree.
qa sends `session evict <client id>` (bare numeric filter, pre-Octopus form) through the admin socket; the parser takes it as id and stops parsing; a bare 0 matches every client.

rust_implications.topic: Two transports, one async command router
rust_implications.implication: Implement both the Unix admin socket framing (NUL/newline-terminated JSON, 4-byte BE length reply, ERROR: prefix) and MCommand/MCommandReply with tid echo and Linux errno mapping. Run every command as an async task routed to the owning shard; never block a transport thread (C++ blocks its single admin thread in osdmap barrier, session kill, tag path, lockup and in every local asok async command).

Return get_command_descriptions with descriptors that reproduce the C++ prefixes and argument types for every supported command (CephChoices n=N for scrubops so the CLI splits commas, CephBool flags, '--' named-only args for quiesce db), otherwise the stock ceph CLI cannot send tell/daemon commands at all.

Ignore unknown keys in the cmdmap (mgr/volumes sends its whole kwargs dict with quiesce db) and enforce required scalar args with -EINVAL; decide deliberately whether empty vector args (session evict without filters) may mean 'all'.

Minimum surface for unmodified peers: get_command_descriptions/help, 0/version, counter dump, counter schema, config show (pid_file), perf dump, config get/set, injectargs, dump_mempools, heap stats (may return -EOPNOTSUPP), session ls/client ls, session evict/client evict, quiesce db, quarantine enable/disable, status, scrub start/status/abort/pause/resume, damage ls/rm, flush journal, dump_ops_in_flight/ops; rotate-key optional (cephadm path dormant).

client ls/session ls must emit id, state and client_metadata with every client-provided key (hostname and root always present) plus client_features.feature_bits and metric_spec.metric_flags.feature_bits as '0x'+hex strings; dashboard and mgr/stats index these directly. In a sharded design the listing must be a rank-wide (all shards) view because sessions are per (client, rank).

Keep the order blocklist (mon osd blocklist add) -> wait for OSDMap containing it -> advance osd_epoch_barrier -> close/journal the session; evictions of different sessions can run in parallel. Filters must support id=, auth_name=, client_metadata.<key>=, state=, reconnecting=.

Non-leader MDS must answer -ENOTTY with JSON containing 'leader' (gid) and 'epoch' so mgr/volumes and qa quiescer can retry; leader output schema {epoch, leader, set_version, sets{...}} is passed to users verbatim by `ceph fs quiesce`.

rust_implications.topic: Subvolume-scoped admin commands map to shards
rust_implications.implication: quarantine (subvolume root), qos set/rm/get (subvolume root from client_metadata.root), quiesce db roots (subvolume paths), session evict client_metadata.root filter are naturally per-subvolume; route them to the owning shard/rank instead of failing with -EXDEV as C++ internal ops do (volumes sends quarantine to the first active rank).

Docs, qa and task-status consumers address scrub at mds.<fs>:0 and expect rank 0 to coordinate; whatever scrub coordinator the Rust MDS uses must accept start/abort/pause/resume at rank 0 and report via 'scrub status' task status key and the scrub status JSON shape (status string, scrubs{tag}, return_code in scrub start).

Preserve observable conventions where peers rely on them (scrub start rc 0 with JSON return_code is relied on by qa; quiesce db JSON on error; quarantine JSON on error); C++ quirks such as qos set return_code 1 = success, positive errno from dump cache, dropped error JSON when r<0 are not relied on by peers and need not be copied.

Dumps (dump cache, dump tree, get subtrees, openfiles ls, session ls, dump loads) must not stall request processing; use per-shard snapshots/streaming with time bounds instead of holding a global lock (C++ holds mds_lock for the whole dump, bounded by mds_beacon_interval/2).

rust_implications.topic: flush journal semantics for sharded journals
rust_implications.implication: Operators and qa use flush journal to make all metadata durable in its home location and trim the journal; with per-shard journals this means flushing and checkpointing every shard and returning {message, return_code} once all are done. C++ offline tools will not work against the new format anyway.

status must report 'state' matching the MDSMap state string (qa wait_for_daemons checks up:active), plus whoami, id, fs_name, epochs and replay progress fields used by troubleshooting docs (replay_status).

Must broadcast CEPH_SESSION_FORCE_RO to all client sessions and revoke write caps; kernel clients rely on it to fail writes with -EROFS. Read-only should be a rank (or shard) mode that also blocks exports, fragmentation and journal flushes.
Push MMgrReport task_status {'scrub status': summary} while scrubbing and clear it afterwards so ceph -s shows scrub progress.

rust_implications.topic: Test hooks for the lock manager
rust_implications.implication: qa relies on lock path (lock names quiesce/snap/policy/file/nest/dft/auth/link/xattr/flock with r/w/x), quiesce path, op get/op kill to construct conflicts; a Hierarchical Lock Manager needs equivalent hooks (or qa must be adapted) and such held ops should not count as slow requests.

Implement the CephContext-style commands (perf dump/schema, counter dump/schema, config show/get/set/unset/diff, injectargs, log reopen, dump_mempools) because exporter, telemetry, qa and operators use them; log rotation uses SIGHUP to a process named ceph-mds.

Map each C++ mds_lock-protected command to its real scope: session (session ls/evict/config), inode/dirfrag (dump inode/dir, dirfrag split/merge, flush_path), subtree (export dir, quarantine, quiesce), journal shard (flush journal), global-but-read-only (dumps), true rank-wide (force_readonly, cache drop).

rust_implications.topic: Do not inherit C++ crash and leak paths
rust_implications.implication: Return errors instead of aborting where C++ asserts or aborts on admin input: cache drop with a failing journal flush (formatter double close), lock path without --await on any failure (no finisher), and the quiesce path use-after-free. Commands should always produce a reply or a negative rc.

Decide deliberately whether an fsname-restricted 'allow *' may administer other file systems' MDS daemons (C++ allows it because allow_all ignores fsname); mgr and client.admin carry unrestricted 'allow *', so enforcing fsname does not break stock peers.

Reproduce the JSON formatter's behaviour of dropping the outermost section name (bare arrays for session ls/get subtrees, bare objects elsewhere) because mgr/stats, dashboard and qa parse those shapes; quirks nobody relies on (scrub resume return_code 1, empty output from dump stray) may be normalized.

open_questions: Rook MDS liveness probe: does it use the admin socket (status) or tell? Rook source is not in this tree (unverified).

mgr/volumes sends quarantine enable|disable to the first active rank (normally rank 0) and its comment claims the MDS forwards; internal ops complete with -EXDEV when the rank is not auth for the subvolume root inode. This only works while rank 0 owns the /volumes/<group> dirfrag holding the subvolume dentry; is a group pinned to another rank supported?
Is the dead scrub_path registration (always -ENOSYS) intended to remain? Any external tool still sending scrub_path?
doc/cephfs/eviction.rst shows `client evict client_metadata.=4305`, which the current SessionFilter parser rejects; docs are outdated or parser regressed?
session evict with an empty filters list (raw JSON/libcephfs) evicts all clients of the rank; is this relied on anywhere or an accident of validate_cmd treating vector args as optional?
cephadm _rotate_daemon_key (tell rotate-key) has no caller and `orch daemon rotate-key` is disabled in this release; will it be re-enabled (making rotate-key peer-critical again)?
dmClock QoS settings (qos set) are in-memory per rank and keyed by session mount root; is persistence or cluster-wide propagation expected by any mgr module in future?
Is an fsname-restricted 'allow *' MDS cap meant to permit tell commands to MDS daemons of other file systems (MDSCapMatch::is_match_all ignores fs_name)?
Are the cache drop formatter assert (journal flush failure) and the lock path abort without --await known upstream bugs? Both are inferred from code, not reproduced.
